clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old male presented with fatigue, abdominal distension, and leg edema. Initial workup revealed elevated tumor markers (CEA, CA 19-9) and a large right atrial mass (6.2 × 3.3 cm) on TTE, causing severe tricuspid insufficiency and IVC dilation. A resection of the right atrial mass was performed. Histopathological evaluation of this excision material confirmed the diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma metastasis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms of fluid overload: fatigue, abdominal distension, and leg edema.
Physical examination showed signs of fluid overload: abdominal dullness to percussion, decreased breath sounds at lung bases, and significant pretibial edema.
Initial laboratory tests revealed elevated tumor markers: CEA 43 ng/mL and CA 19-9 361 U/mL.
Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) identified a large right atrial mass (6.2 × 3.3 cm) near the tricuspid valve, with dilation of the inferior vena cava and severe tricuspid insufficiency.
Resection of the right atrial mass was performed.
Histopathological evaluation of the excision material from the right atrial mass revealed gastric adenocarcinoma metastasis.
